title: What Protein Computing Is
definition: Protein Computing: logic executed by folding proteins.
description:
Strip Protein Computing to its essence and you get logic executed by folding proteins. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Future Computing Paradigms: first folding logic understanding, then protein logistics prototypes, then design tools operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of protein hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

title: 2030 — First protein hulls cloud instances rent folding logic logic by
definition: 2030 milestone on the Protein Computing roadmap.
description:
First protein hulls cloud instances rent folding logic logic by the hour to researchers worldwide.

What must be true first: the folding logic results have to replicate outside the lab, protein logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and design tools operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed folding logic demonstrations, protein logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting design tools uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Protein Computing
definition: Estimates Protein Computing readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Protein Computing components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a protein hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Protein Computing Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Protein Computing operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Protein Computing installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 77698 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where folding logic monitoring, protein logistics redundancy, or design tools maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Protein Computing Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Protein Computing: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Protein Computing — logic executed by folding proteins.

Phase 1 — Prove (folding logic): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (protein logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (design tools): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (readout assays): protein hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and biolabs-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
